These are required observable properties of the implementation, not properties of its returned aggregation list alone.","attempted_representations":["Use an Input record with events:List Event, start:Int, end:Int, width:Int and fill:String; Event has group:String, time:Int and value:Option Int. Return List Row, with group:String, start:Int, count:Nat and value:Option Int. Apply the specified validity guard without additional caller assumptions. This preserves the JSON object keys and raw null-or-integer values, but records do not observe Python module exports or execution effects.","Compute sorted unique groups from every event; enumerate bucket indices using list_range with int_to_nat of floor((end-start+width-1)/width) under the positive-width guard. For each group, fold buckets with an accumulator containing previous:Option Int and rows:List Row, initially absent and empty. Filter event occurrences by group, bucket boundaries and non-null value; count occurrences and sum their integer payloads. Nonempty buckets set previous to Some sum, including zero; empty buckets preserve previous. This faithfully represents aggregation, ordering, duplicates and causal filling, but cannot establish the operational parts of O1.","Adding an effects or entry-point field to the returned record would change the specified output and only report a value supplied by the implementation; it would not observe actual effects or exports. A separate symbol carrying such a report would likewise have no registered connection to Python execution."]},{"obligation_ids":["R1"],"feature":"Executable observation of external I/O and required Python facilities","reason":"No admitted term or formula observes external I/O performed during execution or the implementation's imported and required facilities. Consequently the language cannot express that the actual Python implementation uses exclusively standard-library facilities and performs no external I/O while preserving the required output structure.","attempted_representations":["An inline primitive reference expression built from records, options, scalar arithmetic, filtering and total folds has no modeled I/O operation. Comparing solve(input) with that expression constrains returned values, but implementations with identical values can differ in actual I/O and third-party dependencies.","Encoding an import list or I/O trace as additional output fields or a Result wrapper changes the required List Row output and does not establish that those reports match execution. Encoding them as independent symbols lacks any primitive observing the real implementation.","A raw Lean operational model would require an executable bridge connecting module loading, facility use and external effects to actual Python execution. Such observations are not registered in the supplied bridge, and opaque Lean acceptance cannot satisfy the requested TESTED assurance."]}]}
